key_insight: Variance-guided measurement group construction (VGMC) reduces molecular energy estimation variance by redesigning which Pauli terms share measurements, rather than only optimizing existing measurement bases.
engineering_relevance: VGMC offers a route to lower sampling costs for variational quantum simulations while retaining local measurements compatible with current and near-term devices.
method: Include every Hamiltonian term measurable in each existing basis, then jointly optimize estimator coefficients and shot allocations.
Score candidate groups by their variance benefit relative to the cost of withdrawing shots from existing bases.
Greedily construct qubit-wise commuting groups and jointly re-optimize the expanded measurement design.
evidence_signal: With exact covariances, VGMC reduced variance by 18.19%–23.38% versus state-of-the-art methods on molecular benchmarks where it added bases; gains persisted with approximate covariances, and finite-shot simulations indicated lower shot requirements near chemical accuracy.
watch_item: Practical savings depend on covariance estimation quality, and the abstract does not establish hardware-level benefits after accounting for covariance acquisition and classical optimization overhead.
paper_title: From optimization to construction: Expanding quantum measurement designs
